Subject: Evaluation & MAP request — Cross-cloud private offers

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our procurement team asked me to confirm the path to close across all three clouds (AWS/Azure/GCP). Can Redwood support a staged private-offer approach (we want AWS first, then Azure, then GCP) while keeping a single point of billing reconciliation on our side?

Specifically we need:
- A mutual action plan that lists milestone owners and dates for acceptance tests across the three clouds
- PO / contract template for private offers and any expected addenda for marketplace commitments
- Typical timelines you’ve seen for enterprise customers doing staged marketplace commitments (any gating items we should expect from our legal/finance teams)

Procurement has looped in the queue (procurement@cloudbridge.com) — CC’d. Mike (CTO) is also watching the timeline.

Could you send a draft MAP and the PO template? Our target for first-PO execution is mid-Jan (ideally Jan 15).

Best,
Jane

Jane — thanks, and great to meet everyone. Attached is a first-pass MAP (RBW_CloudBridge_MAP_v1.pdf) and a PO template (RBW-PO-Template.docx). High-level notes:

1) Staggered approach works well. We usually do AWS private offer first because of faster procurement turnarounds in most large enterprise buyers. Azure marketplace commitment typically requires an acceptance checklist (security & usage limits) and can take 2–3 weeks after PO; GCP private offer has similar acceptance gating but often needs additional billing-account setup (can be parallelized).

2) Proposed milestone cadence (draft):
- Week 0 (submission): Signed PO for AWS private offer -> Redwood provisioned in dedicated pool -> customer completes acceptance tests (1–3 days)
- Week 1–2: Azure commitment paperwork + legal signoff (customer finance)
- Week 2–4: GCP private offer acceptance + billing link setup

3) Billing path options (pick one):
- Per-cloud invoices (default): separate invoices per marketplace and standard finance reconciliation
- Consolidated invoicing via a single Marketplace aggregator (requires CloudBridge finance to approve aggregator flow; we can provide examples)
- Direct invoicing (Redwood invoice) if CloudBridge requires a single vendor invoice — note this requires an enterprise billing addendum and may affect marketplace incentives.

4) Action owners: we filled suggested owners in the attached MAP. Karthik will lead the cloud-specific engineering acceptance lanes; Naomi will manage billing & finance coordination. I’ve marked critical decision points that will block rollouts.

Next steps:
- Please review the MAP and the PO template; if procurement confirms the preferred billing path we’ll finalize the DocuSign-ready PO and lock dates.
- If Jan 15 is still the target, we should have signed PO for AWS by 2027-01-10 to allow provisioning and acceptance before cutover.

Thanks — attaching both files to this thread.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: RBW_CloudBridge_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP draft), RBW-PO-Template.docx (PO template)

Looping in some engineering acceptance detail for CloudBridge’s team — Jane, quick tech notes to include in the MAP acceptance section:

- Acceptance tests we recommend: basic generation latency under 95th percentile SLA, token-cost sanity checks with your sample prompts, and SSO/KMS integration verification (for Private deployments).
- For AWS private offer: we can provision a dedicated node pool within 24–48 hours of PO/commitment and give you a short runbook to execute the acceptance cases.
- For Azure: prepare an Admin role for our team so we can validate marketplace commitment entitlements (this is the usual gating item).
- For GCP: we expect billing-account linkage takes the longest; recommend having your billing admin pre-authorize Redwood’s marketplace account so we can verify in parallel.

I’ve added specific test cases to the attached acceptance-criteria.xlsx (see sheet: "Core Acceptance"). Priyom/Naomi: we should highlight the two red lines (KMS and billing linkage) as blockers in the MAP.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Jane — quick answers and confirmation:

1) Consolidated invoicing: we have two patterns we’ve used before and I’ve summarized them in the MAP (appendix B). Short summary:
- Aggregated marketplace billing via an approved aggregator: reduces reconciliation work but can change the timing of credits; we’ve used this with two enterprises where finance accepted a single monthly aggregated invoice.
- Redwood direct single-vendor invoicing: requires an enterprise billing addendum and escalated procurement approval; discounts are handled on the Redwood invoice side rather than marketplace credits.

We’ll provide two short references (customers that used aggregator flow) and an anonymized sample reconciliation at your request. Naomi — can you add the sample reconciliation note to the Drive folder?

2) PO template is DocuSign-ready; I can drop the DocuSign wrapper once procurement confirms the billing path and redlines. The marketplace addenda are called out in section 3 of the template (see attached).

3) Recommended immediate actions to hit Jan 15 AWS target:
- By 2027-01-04: CloudBridge to confirm billing path and return PO redlines (procurement)
- By 2027-01-06: Redwood to provide DocuSign PO and schedule provisioning (we will need the billing account alias and contact)
- By 2027-01-10: Signed PO (AWS) so we can provision and run acceptance tests ahead of Jan 15
\If you’d like, we can set a short 30-min sync (this week) with procurement + finance to walk the MAP and payment flows.

I'll upload the references and the sample reconciliation to the Drive link and update the MAP appendix.

Thanks and happy New Year — we’ll move quickly once we have the preferred billing path.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
